There were 87 locations listed, if I remember correctly. Google Maps has a great feature where you can import spreadsheet data with addresses in one of the columns to make a custom map, so I did that. Then I started using Google to look up the phone numbers.

The first thing I noticed is that some of the addresses don't exist -- like it will say "Suite 213" or something, and the actual building has Suite 200 right next to Suite 300. I also noticed, as others have observed, that a lot of the phone numbers / addresses are associated with lawyers, dentists, elder care, and other businesses that have certainly come up in pizzagate contexts.

But here's the thing: at least 80% of the addresses (again, I only checked the Albuquerque ones) could be found directly with a simple Google search on the phone number. In fact, even the ones with nonexistent addresses had those exact nonexistent addresses listed out there in searchable webspace. In addition, at least 80% of the Albuquerque addresses are associated with the name Joseph: either the business owner has the first name Joseph, the Doctor's office is associated with a St. Josephs, etc.

It still might be interesting to look into some of the people and places involved, and I'm not saying that there couldn't be something sinister going on. Heck, maybe the data is deliberately 80% garbage, to hide the ones that are associated with actual criminals. But one thing I will say is that this data really does look like computers fuckin' up.

Maybe a worthwhile way forward for me would be to take the ones that don't appear to be duplicates of data found elsewhere on the web and investigate those.
